description: It sounds disgusting but it's so, soooo good. Especially in ma la hot pots. I don't get to eat this stuff often but when I do, I definitely get my money's worth.

The recipe for a nice Beef Stew: - 3 Medium Potatoes, peeled and chopped. - 3 Carrots, chopped. - 1/2 Kg of Beef, cubed. - 3 cloves of garlic, chopped or crushed. - 2 large onions, chopped. - 1/2 pint of Guinness (or more). - 2 tbsp of Flour. - 1/2 pint of Beef Stock - Salt & Pepper to taste.  Stick a bit of olive oil in the bottom of a large stewing pot, heat it up until it's nice and hot and then put in the beef and then shortly afterwards the onions. Leave this to cook for a few minutes before adding the garlic and then the flour.  Now add the Guinness and stock along with the Potatoes and Carrots, salt and pepper to taste. Give it a good mix then leave it to cook on a medium heat. It'll take at least an hour before the "stewey magic" takes place.

title: 朝州式鱼头锅 Teochew Fish Hotpot - Yum Cha Inn
description: 朝州式鱼头锅 Teochew Fish Hotpot - Yum Cha Inn AUD28.80 --- Mum wanted to try this relatively new Malaysian Chinese restaurant, Yum Cha Inn. OUr first impressions of the menu was that it was indeed Chinese food with a Malaysian slant, including Thai-style dishes and dishes with belacan. The 泰式鸡 Thai-Style Chicken had a good Thai-style salad topping with crushed lemongrass, Kaffir Lime Leaves, and I think some Daun Kesom/Vietnamese Mint to give it a Malaysian twist. Given the option, I would have preferred the milder red onions and maybe some bean sprouts for extra crunch. The 朝州式鱼头锅 Teochew Fish Hotpot was a bit of a waste of a good fish soup. You might expect to find a little hint of chilli to pep up a fish soup, but we fished out 3 or 4 whole chillies that made the soup red hot despite the lack of any signs! The food overall was good, but not fantastic, but I'd probably go back to try their hawker fare, like KL Hokkien Noodles or Fried Kway Teow. We bumped into Chen Chen and Boon Chew a while back after their lunch there one day, and they said they just had yumcha there and wasn't impressed. The food was nothing special and a tad pricey. And yes, the food, especially the specials are a bit on the high side. 粗茶馆 Yum Cha Inn 269 Springvale Rd Glen Waverley 3150 (03) 9803 5632 Photos: - Shop front - Mum, Aunt Lee Geok, Alpha, Julia, Julia's Dad - 龙须豆腐 Dragon Beard Homemade Tofu - AUD18.80 - 马拉盏双豆 French Beans and Okra with Belacan - AUD15.80 - 泰式鸡 Thai-Style Chicken - AUD15.80 - 朝州式鱼头锅 Teochew Fish Hotpot - AUD28.80 - 椰汁糕 Coconut Pudding - complimentary

title: stewy goodness
description: Vegetable Stew  1/3 of a medium turnip 4 middling sized carrots 4 stalks celery 2 large red potatoes 1 small acorn squash 1/4 of a large vidalia onion Cut up and throw into a dutch oven with peas green beans corn  Make veg broth with 1 TB "better than bullion" and 3 cups hot water, pour into pot Season with salt, pepper, Bell's, rosemary & garlic Cover and put into 350 degree oven When carrots are softish take out 1 cup of broth, add 2 TB flour and 2 TB butter. Mix until smooth and add back into the pot. Stir until combined with the rest of the liquid, don't over stir or you will have veg mush. Turn off oven and put pot back in for another 1/2 hour or so until the broth has thickened.  EAT!

title: Spicy Hot Pot
description: Mr. Moc and I love eating spicy foods so last weekend we had taiwanese-style spicy hot pot (aka shabu shabu).   For those of you who don't know what hot pot ("huo-guo") is ....basically you have a pot of broth simmering on a burner on the table. To the pot, you add thinly sliced meat (beef, pork, chicken, etc.), seafood, veggies, fish balls, dumplings, tofu and/or whatever else you like and let it cook. Once an ingredient is cooked, you scoop it out and dip it in a sauce and eat.   Since we like spicy, our broth was made of a very spicy paste that made our noses run!

A bowl of "healthy" rice (it's got black rice in it?) accompanied the stew, but I was only able to dig half way as there was probably a whole bowl of rice in my hot stone pot. title: black eyed bean veggie stew
description: Recipe (for theSeuss)  Although I just made it up as I went along.  This was done in one of those slow cooker things:  1 large onion chopped and fried until nice and soft in olive oil first Then add 2 cloves of crushed garlic.  Chopped into chunks: 1 turnip or Swede 1 large potato 3 or 4 large carrots 1 green pepper  1 tin of chopped tomatoes 1 tin of black eyed beans 2 vegetable OXO stock cubes About a tablespoon of olive oil A cup of hot water  The whole lot put into a pot and stirred together.  Then leave to simmer gently on a low heat for 45 minutes to an hour or until the veggies are cooked through.

title: One of my regular meals and a family favorite: Jean Food!
description: We call this Jean Food, as our family friend Jean taught me the recipe.  It's really easy (like foolproof easy).  Just sautee zucchini and italian sausage while a pot of penne is cooking.  Then add a can of stewed or diced tomatoes (my favorite brand for this particular recipe is Del Monte).  Let it all simmer together, add a sprinkle of parm, and you're good to go.    You can easily add onion, mushrooms, spinach, or fresh mozz as well--but the basic recipe is lovely and filling, and it's just as delicious both hot right off the stove as well as cold the next day for lunch.
